maisonNous.noteFin: This quiz is a game: it gives you an idea, not property advice. The photos were created for this page.
maisonNous.p_pavillon_d: A house of your own, on a quiet street, with a bit of garden, a barbecue and room to store things. It's the choice of couples who want to settle down, have friends over on Saturdays and see the family grow without moving. It's not the most original one, but it's probably the most comfortable.
maisonNous.p_pavillon_a: Look at the commute: a house with a garden is often further from work and from nights out. Do the drive on a Monday morning before you commit.
maisonNous.p_appartement_d: Everything is within walking distance: the bakery, the cinema, the restaurants, your friends. You'd rather have a balcony overlooking the rooftops than a lawn to mow, and you have no wish to spend your weekends doing DIY. You'll have fewer square feet, and far more life around you.
maisonNous.p_appartement_a: The two things to talk about are noise and the lack of outdoor space. View it in the evening and at the weekend, not just on a Tuesday at 3 p.m.
maisonNous.p_campagne_d: Old stone, shutters, a vegetable patch, and silence in the evening. You want space, to watch the seasons go by, and to potter around outside on Sundays. Friends will come for the weekend, and they'll find it hard to leave.
maisonNous.p_campagne_a: In the countryside you often need a car each, and the doctor isn't always round the corner. Rent there for a winter before you buy.
maisonNous.p_loft_d: A former factory, huge windows, brick walls, and one big room where everything happens. You love the city, big open spaces and evenings that end late at your place. Small closed-off rooms are not for you.
maisonNous.p_loft_a: No walls also means not much privacy. If one of you goes to bed early and the other doesn't, plan at least one real bedroom. And ask to see the heating bill.
maisonNous.p_architecte_d: Straight lines, big picture windows, and nothing out of place. You have precise tastes, you don't like building work that drags on, and you're ready to pay for it. It's a house you design for yourselves, not one you adapt.
maisonNous.p_architecte_a: Agree on the budget before you meet the architect, not after: this is the project where the bill climbs fastest.
maisonNous.p_tiny_d: Two hundred square feet of wood at the edge of a forest, and nothing you don't need. You'd take freedom over floor space, you own very little, and living on top of each other doesn't scare you. In the evening, two chairs outside and a string of lights are enough.
maisonNous.p_tiny_a: Try it first: rent one for a week, in winter if you can. And look into the land, because you can't park it just anywhere.
maisonNous.p_renover_d: Ivy, broken shutters, scaffolding: you can already see your home in it. You like projects that last for years, dust doesn't scare you, and you'd rather redo everything your way than buy something finished. One day it will be gorgeous.
maisonNous.p_renover_a: Renovations put couples to the test. Get a quote before you buy, double the schedule, and keep one liveable room where you can catch your breath.
maisonNous.p_van_d: Your home has four wheels and the view changes every morning. All you need is a bed, a camping stove, and each other. Furniture and a twenty-five-year mortgage can wait, maybe forever.
maisonNous.p_van_a: Start with a month's rental before you sell everything. And keep an address somewhere, if only for the post.
maisonNous.p_peniche_d: Living on the water, right in the city or close to it, with a deck full of plants, bikes on board and ducks for neighbours. You want a place like no other, and a bit of rocking doesn't bother you.
maisonNous.p_peniche_a: A houseboat needs upkeep, and a mooring has to be paid for. Go and talk to people who live on one before you take the plunge.
maisonNous.p_palier_d: Together, but each in your own place. One of you needs their own space, their own hours or their own mess, maybe both of you do, and you don't see why loving each other should mean sharing a bathroom. Two doors, two doormats, and you meet up for dinner.
maisonNous.p_palier_a: It works really well for some couples, as long as it's what you both want. If one of you dreams of living together, say so openly.
